answers.question: is the peer set fairly chosen, and are the peers themselves expensive rather than this being cheap?
answers.answer: I cannot tell. The prospectus states an industry average PE of 128.11, against which the IPO at 51.6x looks like a 60% discount — but zero peer rows could be parsed from what I was given, so I have no idea who those peers are, whether they are genuine comparables, or whether 128x simply means the chosen peers are themselves in a bubble. A 60% discount to an inflated peer set is not cheap; it is just less expensive than an expensive list. This is exactly the kind of benchmark a seller's document would choose to flatter the issue, so I would not rely on it without the underlying peer table.
answers.citation: not answerable from what I was given

answer.what_would_change_my_mind: The actual peer table behind the 128.11 average, plus balance-sheet leverage, ROE/ROCE, and the QIB-versus-retail split of the 61.9x subscription — clean peers, moderate debt, and double-digit ROCE would move my long-term score up materially; a cherry-picked peer set or heavy leverage would push it below 30.
